newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Moss Bros maintains margins.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Moss Bros maintains margins.

text.p: British menswear retailer Moss Bros Group Plc continues to see a "quite fierce" competitive retail market but is maintaining its margins, finance director Terry Donovan said in a telephone interview with Reuters.
"We have not sacrificed our margins in getting a same store sales rise of 14 percent in the first half," he said.
Donovan added that in the first eight weeks of the second half, like-for-like sales were up 11 percent.
Moss Bros said pretax profits for the first half jumped 54 percent to 4.94 million stg and paid out an interim dividend of 6.5 pence, up from five pence previously.
Donovan said the company intended to invest seven to eight million stg in capital expenditure this year but would be concentrating on organic growth.
"At the moment, we are concentrating on organic growth...there is a lot of market share we have yet to be able to take," he said.
But he added that if a suitable acquisition appeared, the company would look at the possibilities.
Moss Bros bought Blazer, a middle-market clothing chain, from Storehouse Plc for 7.1 million stg in June.
Donovan said the company saw potential for around 50 Blazer sites in total in the UK from a current 24 while the rest of the chain could expand by another 30 outlets.
The company has opened 40 new shops in the last 20 months, Donovan added.
